useCase.name: Produce the challan a family takes to the bank, printable by the family themselves

intent.name: fee.challan.generate
intent.summary: Produce the bank challan for issued, unpaid invoices — one invoice, a class, a section, or a whole issue batch. One per invoice, and it moves no money.

request.gloss: the money has come in, record it

routesElsewhere.note: Printing a challan moves no money and changes no invoice (BR-9). Recording what came back from the bank is a different act.
A challan is produced against an invoice that already exists.

request.text: dono bhai behno ka ek hi challan bana do
request.gloss: make one challan for both siblings

routesElsewhere.note: One challan covers one invoice. A single reference has to tie the bank payment back to the exact invoice (BR-3, BR-4), and a slip covering several children returns one total that cannot be split across their invoices without a guess — which is what UC-04-05 BR-3 exists to prevent.
Generating and sending are different acts.

request.gloss: change the amount on the challan

routesElsewhere.note: Every figure is taken from the invoice and nothing on it is typed, so the slip and the ledger cannot disagree (BR-2).

steps.note: One step, producing one challan per unpaid invoice in scope. Every figure comes from the invoice (BR-2), and reprinting returns the same challan with the same reference rather than a new one (BR-7).

plan.onFailure: Stop and report. A paid or cancelled invoice, and missing bank details, are enforced by the API and arrive as errors. Paid invoices inside a class, section or batch scope are skipped and listed rather than aborting the run (E5).
plan.atomicity: A document, not a transaction. No money moves, no invoice changes and no ledger entry is made (BR-9). What is written is a challan record per invoice with its own unique reference, and the generation entry, so a slip circulating in a family's hands can be traced to when it was produced and by whom (BR-11). Reprinting returns the existing challan rather than issuing a second reference — two references for one bill is how a payment gets entered twice (BR-7).

operations.name: fee.challan.generate
operations.idempotencyKey: invoice_id — one invoice carries one challan, and BR-7 backs it: reprinting produces the same reference, never a second
operations.purpose: Produce one challan per issued, unpaid invoice in scope, in its bank, school and payer copies, or return the ones that already exist.

parameters.name: scope
parameters.notes: One invoice, every unpaid invoice of a class or section, or every unpaid invoice of one issue batch. A batch is exactly one issue run, so the billing period is unambiguous — which a class scope on its own is not (see the open question).

parameters.name: invoice_id

resolves.onNoMatch: Refuse. No issued, unpaid invoice matches.
resolves.onAmbiguous: Ask, naming the candidates with student, period and balance.

parameters.notes: Required where the scope is Student.

parameters.name: class_id

resolves.onNoMatch: Refuse. No active class of that name.

parameters.notes: Required where the scope is Class. Covers every unpaid invoice of that class, across whatever periods are outstanding — report how many and for which periods before printing.

parameters.name: section_id
parameters.notes: Required where the scope is Section.

parameters.name: batch_id

resolves.onAmbiguous: Ask, naming the candidates with batch number, scope, period, invoice count and how many are still unpaid.

parameters.notes: Required where the scope is Batch. The invoice run to print for — one run, one period, one unambiguous set of invoices.

parameters.name: branch_id
parameters.notes: Never from the request, even where the request names a campus or a past year (branch-scope, academic-session-scope).

returns.description: The challans produced, or the ones that already existed.

fields.name: challans
fields.description: challan_reference, invoice_number, student, amount_payable, due_date — one per unpaid invoice.

fields.name: challan_reference
fields.description: Unique per challan. It is what ties the eventual bank payment back to the exact invoice (BR-3).

fields.name: amount_payable
fields.description: Taken from the invoice. Never typed (BR-2).

fields.name: payable_after_due_date
fields.description: The higher amount where a late fee policy applies, printed alongside (BR-8).

fields.name: copies
fields.description: Bank, school and payer — identical in content (BR-5).

fields.name: generated_count
fields.description: How many challans the run produced.

fields.name: skipped_paid
fields.description: Invoices in scope already paid, skipped and listed (E5).

fields.name: reprinted
fields.description: Those that already had a challan and were returned unchanged (BR-7).

fields.name: periods_covered
fields.description: For a class or section scope, which billing periods the unpaid invoices span. Report this — it is the ambiguity a batch scope avoids.

errors.meaning: The invoice has already been paid.
errors.note: The message names the payment date. A family is never sent to the bank with a slip for a bill that has been paid (BR-1).

errors.meaning: The charge has been cancelled or credited.
errors.note: Message: "This charge has been cancelled. There is nothing to pay."

errors.meaning: No bank details are configured for the branch.
A guardian requested a challan for a child who is not theirs.
Some invoices in the scope have already been paid.
errors.notWritten: No challan for the paid ones.
errors.note: Listed and skipped. Not a failure — a batch printed a week after issue will usually contain some.

errors.meaning: The challan could not be rendered.
errors.note: Message: "The challan could not be generated. Please try again."

planningRules.rule: Never type a figure onto a challan. Every amount, the due date and the after-due-date amount are taken from the invoice so the slip and the ledger cannot disagree (BR-2), and there is no parameter for any of them.
Never treat a reprint as a new challan. Reprinting returns the same reference (BR-7); two references for one bill is how a payment gets entered twice, and the bank quotes whichever slip it is handed.

Never combine invoices onto one slip. One challan covers one invoice, because one reference has to tie the bank payment back to the exact invoice (BR-3, BR-4) — a combined slip returns one total that could only be split across invoices by guessing, which UC-04-05 BR-3 forbids outright.

Prefer a batch scope over a class scope, and report the periods when a class scope is used. A batch is one issue run and so one period; a class may hold unpaid invoices from several, and printing them all hands a family three slips they did not expect.
Never generate a challan for a paid or cancelled invoice to 'have one on file'. A family holding a slip will take it to the bank, and E1 and E2 refuse it for that reason.
Never chain a payment record onto a challan. Printing moves no money (BR-9); the payment is recorded when the stamped school copy comes back, which may be days later.

reversal.statement: A challan is a document and is not withdrawn. It becomes unusable when its invoice is paid or cancelled, and the bank copy returned afterwards is what closes it (BR-10). Where a slip is circulating for a charge that has since been cancelled, nothing recalls it — the bank will simply find no open invoice against the reference.

request.text: Ayesha ka September ka challan nikaal do

resolvedPlans.context: Accounts, Johar Town branch, on an issued unpaid invoice of PKR 5,000 due 10-09-2026.

steps.note: No amount is supplied — every figure comes from the invoice (PR-1).

resolvedPlans.outcome: One challan with a unique reference, PKR 5,000 payable by 10-09-2026 and the higher amount payable after it, in bank, school and payer copies. Nothing moved and the invoice is unchanged.

request.text: jo batch abhi issue kiya hai, us ke saare challan print kar do
request.gloss: print all the challans for the batch we just issued

resolvedPlans.context: Accounts, Johar Town branch, on a batch of 30 invoices issued this morning.

steps.note: A batch is one run and one period, so which invoices are printed is unambiguous — unlike a class scope (PR-4).

resolvedPlans.outcome: 30 challans, one per invoice, each with its own reference. Report the count. Where any had already been paid since issue they are skipped and listed (E5).

request.text: poori Grade 4 ke challan nikaal do
request.gloss: produce the challans for the whole of Grade 4

resolvedPlans.context: Accounts, Johar Town branch, in November. Some students have unpaid September, October and November invoices.

steps.note: A class scope covers every unpaid invoice, whatever the period. periods_covered comes back naming all three (PR-4).

resolvedPlans.outcome: 68 challans across three billing periods for 30 students. Report that before handing them out — the actor probably meant this month's batch, and some families would otherwise receive three slips.
